title: Canonical coefficient factor at the named raw-complex endpoints
statement: For a commutative ring Λ, a module sheaf G on a scheme W, any integer q and an arrow f:A→B over W, give moduleCoefficientFactor(Λ,G,q,A,B,f) [def-sbc-raw-scalar-coefficient-factors] its equivalent type from the derived inverse image under f.left of higherDirectImageRawOverComplex(Λ,G,B)[q] to higherDirectImageRawOverComplex(Λ,G,A)[q] [def-sbc-higher-image-raw-over-complex]. The typed view is an abbreviation of the canonical morphism itself, not a second construction; unfolded, it is the direct inverse-image shift comparison followed by the shifted higherDirectImageRawOverCoefficient [def-sbc-higher-image-raw-over-coefficient]. No new coefficient object, comparison or choice is made. The heterogeneous computation rule identifies this typed view with that canonical morphism.

source.document: Stacks Project; the existing canonical raw coefficient factor

proof.text: Define the view as the canonical moduleCoefficientFactor at the named raw-complex endpoint types; these types are definitionally equal to the expanded single-complex endpoints, so the abbreviation typechecks. Heterogeneous reflexivity identifies it with the canonical morphism. Unfolding the abbreviation, moduleCoefficientFactor and the moduleUpperStar abbreviation gives the explicit two-factor computation rule by reflexivity. This works for every integer shift, including zero, identity arrows and zero coefficient sheaves. All data and proofs are complete.
